question: When dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate, which of the following observations is correct?

options.text: Formation of a salt and water only
Formation of hydrogen gas with a pop sound
Rapid evolution of a colourless gas that turns lime water milky
Formation of brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide

solution:
The correct answer is __**Rapid evolution of a colourless gas that turns lime water milky​.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl)** reacts with **sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃)**, a chemical reaction occurs, producing **carbon dioxide gas (CO₂)**, water (H₂O), and sodium chloride (NaCl).
 
• The reaction is represented as:

 **NaHCO₃ + HCl → NaCl + H₂O + CO₂**.
 
• The evolution of **CO₂ gas** is rapid and observable as bubbles or effervescence during the reaction.
 
• **Carbon dioxide gas**, when passed through lime water (Ca(OH)₂), reacts to form calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), which turns the lime water milky:

 **CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O**.
 
• This observable change is a key characteristic of the reaction between an acid and a carbonate or bicarbonate compound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Explanation of the incorrect options:**

 
 
• **Formation of a salt and water only:** This is incorrect because the reaction also produces carbon dioxide gas in addition to salt and water.
 
• **Formation of hydrogen gas with a pop sound:** This is incorrect because hydrogen gas is not produced in this reaction. The gas evolved is carbon dioxide.
 
• **Formation of brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide:** This is incorrect because nitrogen dioxide (NO₂) is not involved in this reaction.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of carbon dioxide:**
 
 
• Carbon dioxide is a **colourless, odourless gas**.
 
• It is slightly soluble in water, forming **carbonic acid (H₂CO₃)**.
 
• Its presence can be identified using the **lime water test**, which turns milky due to the formation of calcium carbonate.
 
 
 
• **Applications of bicarbonates:**
 
 
• **Sodium bicarbonate** (baking soda) is widely used in cooking as a leavening agent.
 
• It is also used in **antacids** to neutralize excess stomach acid.
 
• In laboratories, bicarbonates are used to study reactions with acids for educational purposes.
 
 
 
• **Acid-carbonate reactions:**
 
 
• Acid-carbonate or acid-bicarbonate reactions are commonly used to test for the presence of carbonates in substances.
 
• These reactions are exothermic and produce effervescence due to the evolution of carbon dioxide gas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Carbon dioxide detection:**

 
 
• Carbon dioxide can be detected using the **lime water test**, which is a simple yet effective method to confirm its presence.
 
• This test is often used in school laboratories to demonstrate the reaction between acids and carbonates.
 
 
 
• **Environmental significance:**
 
 
• Carbon dioxide is a **greenhouse gas** and plays a significant role in global warming and climate change.
 
• Its concentration in the atmosphere is monitored carefully by scientists to understand and mitigate environmental impacts.
 
 
 
• **Safety precautions:**
 
 
• While performing the reaction in a laboratory, ensure proper ventilation as the rapid evolution of carbon dioxide can displace oxygen momentarily.
 
• Avoid skin contact with hydrochloric acid as it is corrosive and can cause burns.
